items.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary_1line: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) achieve remarkable success on diverse multimodal understanding and generation tasks, yet they still struggle to effectively leverage language-based chain-of-thought reasoning for image...
items.editor_note: Brings continuous-space latent reasoning to unified multimodal models.

editorial.tldr: An Oct 18 paper proposed hybrid agents that reason in latent space but act through text. A paper on Oct 27 then applied latent reasoning to multi-agent systems by storing reusable skills in compact external memory.
editorial.whats_new: A new arXiv paper moves latent reasoning into continuous space for unified multimodal models, targeting weak language-based chain-of-thought in image tasks.
editorial.why_it_matters: Latent reasoning aims to cut inference cost by keeping intermediate steps out of text, but it also makes those steps harder to inspect and log.
editorial.take_for_builders: These are unreplicated preprints; if you log reasoning traces for debugging, check what your tooling would lose before adopting latent-reasoning models.

open_questions: Do any of these papers report cost or latency savings against text chain-of-thought on the same tasks?
Is code or a model release available for the Hybrid Agents or SkillMem approaches?
